content.text: Crusader Kings II has 161 different achievements , all using the Steam achievements mechanics. Achievements have no in-game effects; the achievement just pops up in-game, and is then added to the player's Steam profile. It is possible to see the achievements sorted by the percentage of users that managed to complete each achievement by going to the game's global achievements at Steam .

The difficulty of each achievement varies; some achievements are very easy (e.g. Marrying another character), while some are more difficult (e.g. Reconquering all historical Roman territories). The below list groups the various achievements by a difficulty level as assessed by the wiki editors.

Achievements can only be gained in single-player Ironman games. You cannot unlock achievements if you used the Ruler Designer to start a campaign. They can be earned while playing older versions of the game as long as said achievements were present in that version. Playing game in offline mode (saving game in offline even once) permanently disables achievements for this savegame. Certain game rules will also disable achievements for the savegame; usually, such rules make the game easier.

It is not possible to gain achievements if the checksum has been changed - either by tampering with game files, or by running the game using mods that affect gameplay mechanics (graphical mods do not affect checksum), or a corrupted installation (the Ironman mode icon will change to reflect this).
The "Notes" column lists helpful short tips/strategies.
The column denotes achievements which can't be completed without the use of DLC mechanics (currently 111 out of 161). Multiple expansion icons mean either can be used.
The Random World or the Shattered World buttons mean that they are mandatory to fulfill the achievement (currently 5 out of 161). For achievements without the icons, the buttons must not be selected.
The Starting conditions column may denote the requirements needed for the player character before the achievement requirements are fulfilled.
The Religion column denotes achievements which can't be completed without the specified religion. (currently 43 out of 161). Multiple religion icons mean either can be used.
The "Ver" column indicates in which version a certain achievement was added. Achievements cannot be earned prior to the version they were added in.
The "DI" column is for difficulty as assessed by wiki editors.

items.text: VE = Very Easy (Can be achieved through normal play or can be achieved in minutes)
E = Easy (Can be achieved easily although might take some time)
M = Medium (Can be achieved by most players although some aspects will be difficult)
H = Hard (Can be achieved in a full campaign or requires difficult to trigger events)
VH = Very Hard (Difficult to achieve and often requires an ahistorical playstyle)
I = Insane (Almost unachievable due to the large amount of work and difficult requirements)

Occasionally an event pops up in counties within the regions of East and West Africa that allows you to perform a rain dance. You will get a success pop up if this works, and if you are or become a King or Emperor while the success is active the achievement will activate. There is no culture or religion requirement and the kingdom or empire title need not be in Africa. You don't even have to pay for the event. You can also revoke or conquer a county under the effect of rain, and you'll get it that way.

Creating the Kingdom of Jerusalem requires Christian religion, but the achievement itself has no religious requirements.
A non-Christian can inherit or usurp the title if it exists. Easily cheesed as Fatimids. You have two easy options to become Christian, which is required to create the kingdom of Jerusalem.
You can either marry a Christian (any religion in the Christian group will work) or move your capital to one of the Miaphysite counties you own and then convert to the local religion (1000 prestige).
Destroy the Shia Caliphate (200 prestige) in order to be able to change religion.
Secretly convert to Christianity using your newly-wed wife, or by right-clicking your portrait if you moved your capital to a Miaphysite county.
Publicly adopt secret religion if you converted secretly.
Create the Kingdom of Jerusalem (250 gold + 200 piety).

All Catholic emperors (there are no Fratricelli emperors) in every start begin the game already crowned, so we're going to start as a non-Catholic emperor. Make sure the Pope isn't in hiding due to disease (as he may be unavailable for several years) then publicly adopt faith. To settle a mercenary they must be your friend. There is an event chain for a hired mercenary to become your friend. It fires for you, not the mercenary leader, so hiring multiple mercenaries does not make it fire faster. It won't fire unless the ruler who sent the mercenary away (generally his father) is still alive, and the mercenary is residing in your capital, which happens when he is removed from leading troops. Once he is your friend, dismiss him and then use the "Settle Adventurer" action on him. This achievement is simple with the Charlemagne and Conclave DLCs.

Take hunting, family, or theology focus for a small health bonus - there's a very good chance you may die of old age before the invasion is over. Raise your vassal fleet levies, and take your army home so you aren't targeted by either England or Normandy. Don't forget to split up your army since the supply limit of your counties is only ~5k, so you don't lose troops. Once William inevitably wins his invasion, return to England and begin assaulting holdings as quickly as possible. Target the ones that William assaulted (the red ones using the economy view). As a result of winning his invasion, William's new holdings will have the "recently conquered" negative modifier which disables that holding's levy for one year, making assaults much easier. You can also marry out your daughter to some prince, and form some alliance that will help you.

Before starting the game, disable Horse Lords (some required territory is held by nomads) and Conclave (to remove 'not on council' vassal opinion malice) to make the game easier. This guide was written without them and some parts may not work or not apply due to mechanics changes if these DLCs are enabled. The first challenge is finding the county of Mohadavasaka - it's in western India on the border of Pratihara and Chawda. Restart until you get a character with high martial. Before unpausing, resign if you're a commander or part of your liege's council so you don't get killed in battle. Immediately divorce your wife and use the character finder to marry someone with high stewardship. Join the Hindu society. Unpause. Next, take the title of your vassal with a castle. First, try plotting to kill him. The plot doesn't actually need to succeed - as long as you have at least one other plotter the plot will eventually be revealed to the target, who will then become a foe that you can duel and kill. If this is taking too long, you can always simply imprison and execute the vassal, but if imprisonment fails and the vassal chooses rebellion, the vassal can easily defeat you by not raising his levy and just waiting out the warscore timer - it is extremely unlikely that your levy will outnumber both your vassal's levy and garrison in the event of a siege. You will want to switch cultures ASAP. Indian rulers can subjugate other rulers within the same group for 500 karma every 100 years per character (unlimited for de jure counties of [X kingdom] if 'Become King of [X]' ambition is set) and if a country flips to your Iranian culture, you will be unable to use the War Elephant Pens cultural building of the Indo-Aryan/Dravidian groups that all of India uses (the Iranian cultural building is the Riding Grounds). Besides Nepali, which can always raid, the differences between Indo-Aryan/Dravidian, and your Iranian culture are based on Culture group which Iranian cultured provinces will be limited in the initial conquests. This also helps in providing you with better relations with other Indo-Aryan/Dravidian characters and keeping cultural buildings rather than Iranian cultural buildings. Raid the Chawda to finance constructing your demesne. Eat up the Pratihara (and the Chawda, if the Pratihara don't force them to become a tributary) with border dispute wars. In the meantime, watch for crown authority to be raised and switch to ultimogeniture succession if it does. Regencies can be dull but it beats having your hard-won realm split apart. From here, you have two options: 1) Usurp or form a duchy, plot to fabricate a claim on the Pratihara kingdom, form a faction to install yourself, and, if possible - spy on your liege, have them kidnapped, then issue your demand and instantly win the war (otherwise issue your demand and fight your liege as usual). Get your state diplomacy as high as possible to attract more plotters. Note that to plot a claim on your liege's title, your primary title must be a duchy that is de jure within your lieges kingdom, which is initally the very small de jure kingdom of Malwa. Your liege controls enough territory at the start to form Rajputana, but you may need to send him gold (375 + 200 piety) until he has enough to do so. or 2) Declare independence - not ideal but may be your only choice if option 1 is unfeasible. After gaining independence, your next goal is to convert to Islam. You will lose your caste once you do so, giving you a large opinion malus with all Hindus, so be sure you can handle the very real possibility of all your vassals revolting simultaneously. Once you're strong enough to resist your neighbors (don't forget to look at their wealth to account for any mercenaries they might hire), raid the Sunnis to your west for a concubine and convert to her religion. You will lose the ability to raid, but the county conquest CB makes this achievement go much faster. The Abbasids and Tagbahlids are close enough that they should assist you in the event of a defensive holy war. Once you become Muslim, pass the medium crown authority law. Revoke all non-Sunni vassals and replace them with more loyal ones, ideally with high martial to give you more levies. Use 'Promote commander' in the intrigue menu to generate good candidates. If you can't afford that, using the 'raise new vassal' option on a city, temple, or castle that you own will create a new noble of your culture and religion. 3 of the counties you need to complete Khotan are owned by the Western Protectorate. Before fighting them, save and quit. Disable Jade Dragon so you don't have to fight China, then resume your game. Defeat the Western Protectorate (they will still retain any tributaries if they had any), then re-enable Jade Dragon if you wish - you no longer need the border dispute CB which is the main reason to leave it enabled in the first place. If Jade Dragon is re-enabled after being disabled, you will lose all grace with China, all Chinese interaction timers will be reset, all trade posts will be destroyed, but any peace deals will remain in effect.

Holy war or de jure claim war any parts of the duchy of Oultrejourdain still outside your realm. Once that's done, use the prestige and piety you earned through the crusade to secretly convert to Jewish through the county of Jerusalem, found the religious cult, prepare ground on Jerusalem, personally adopt faith and then Create Israel.

Start as Caliph Abd-al-Rahman of the Umayyad Empire in The Iron Century bookmark. Join the satanists. Marry a Catholic. None will appear in the arrange marriage menu, so use the character finder to search for unmarried women in your realm not of your religion. The Salihid Emirate to your south may also have eligible candidates. Secretly convert to Catholic via your wife. Make sure the Pope isn't in hiding due to disease (as he may be unavailable for several years) then publicly adopt faith. Organize a coronation ceremony with the Pope and choose the most expensive ceremony option (actually having the money is unnecessary, you are allowed to go into debt for it). Crown yourself.

To convert to Catholicism, either marry a Catholic and secretly convert or revoke the county of Jerusalem and secretly convert via the holy site there. If there are no Catholics in your realm, publicly adopt a religion in the Christian group so that Catholic rulers outside your realm are willing to consider marriage requests. Each decision costs 250 piety and you will have to destroy or give away the Sunni Caliphate title prior to converting. Start as Abbasids in 769.
Diplomatically vassalize at least the Taid Emirate (one of your tributaries).
Then, declare holy war for the duchy of Kabulistan in Bamian, because the Buddhist holy site in the county of Bamian will allow you to secretly convert to Buddhism.
Accumulate 250 piety and 450 prestige; this will allow you to do the next steps quickly and therefore not suffer long from the negative modifiers it will give to your vassals.

When ready, destroy your Caliphate title, leave your society if you're in one, and secretly convert to Buddhism by right-clicking the shield icon of Bamian.
Found the religious cult and use the "Prepare Ground" action on Mecca.
Wait for Mecca to get the "Secret Buddhist Community" modifier (you will get an in-game event).
Finally, openly adopt faith through the decisions menu - "personally adopt faith" in your character's portrait menu will NOT cause counties to convert. If you accidentally personally adopt faith, take a Muslim concubine and convert back to Islam with her, then secretly convert and found the religious cult again - any counties with secret community modifiers will still have them.

Can also be done quickly by settling feudal in the county of Mecca as an Indian religion nomadic horde, if you have .
As a nomad, completely destroying all holdings in Mecca will also change the county's religion.

content.text: As Tughluq in 1337, move your capital within de jure Punjab (or any Indian kingdom you completely control), conquer Mahodayapuram or marry a Nestorian, secretly convert to Nestorian, found the religious cult, prepare ground on your capital, and personally adopt the faith once it gets the "secret Nestorian community" modifier.

Alternatively, you can play as a nomad with HL (Khazaria would be the fastest) and burn the world, so there are fewer and fewer courts (so fewer and fewer characters to slow the game down). With this method you will likely spend a busy 200-300 first years and then you can just set the game at max speed and wait for the end. If you have The Reaper's Due , setting both the Black Death and Minor Epidemics to "Deadly" and "More" respectively will make severe cuts in the number of characters alive, improving performance.

items.text: Before you begin, set the Culture Conversion game rule to "Faster Melting Pots." First, rule French/Occitan/Breton provinces before 1150 to become Norman, then rule Anglo-Saxon provinces in the de jure Kingdom of England after 1100 to become English. Note that you may not get an alert for the English culture event, so keep checking the eligible provinces when the time comes. Note that the culture events can happen in any province in the de jure Kingdom of England, not just the ones you own.

The Petty King of Jorvik in 867, King Halfdan 'Whiteshirt' begins in an invasion of Northumbria and has more event troops (11.6k, 15.6k in total) than Suðreyjar, but has feudal government. You can still subjugate other pagans as long as you have elective gavelkind (which you don't start with, however) and are a pagan yourself. Although the Invasion CB will allow you to take all occupied territory upon successful conclusion of the war, all of Catholic Britannia is likely to join the invasion against you and your ally in Sviþjod who are both Germanic pagans. You get to keep your event troops after the war, so it's recommended to get the war over with quickly and use the Germanic pagan county conquest CB to attack neighboring and coastal counties instead. You can become Norman by ruling the counties of Cornwall or Devon, which are Breton. Note that the English melting pot event will not fire here however, as it's not part of the region of England.

The Petty King of Suðreyjar in 867, King Ivar 'the Boneless', begins with 5.9k event troops (8.2k in total) and in two invasions, one of Northumbria and one of East Anglia. This is a much harder start but Suðreyjar has the benefit of being a tribal government and starting with elective gavelkind.
Suðreyjar and Jorvik are not allied and will not contribute to each other's war score.

Hæsteinn of Retz 867 is another good start, as he can easily take all of Brittany and then prepare an invasion of Western Francia without too much difficulty. If conquering England early, be sure not to eradicate Anglo-Saxon culture before 1100.

Strategy: Although males can use the unholy impregnation decision, the resulting child will be born with an unknown father and will not inherit anything. Therefore, we're going to keep women on the throne. Start as Navarra at any time when it's a single county Kingdom, such as the "Age of the Mongols" bookmark. Set the gender equality game rule to "All". Upon starting, immediately switch to elective monarchy. You have no duke-tier vassals so you will be the sole elector, allowing you to choose your heir freely. Choose a female heir, ideally with many sinful traits and high intrigue in order to gain dark power faster. At society rank 3, you may be given the unholy impregnation mission which allows you to use the decision immediately. Otherwise, you have to reach rank 4 in order to use it freely.

Set the gender equality game rule to 'all' so you have more choice in councilors. Open the character finder and get some better councilors. Switch your succession to elective - barons can't vote, so you have complete control. Imprison and execute the baron of Saint-Pol (your vassal with the castle) until you inherit it (you can't simply revoke it as France has minimal crown authority and is unlikely to raise it). Fabricate claims on and take the counties of Artois and Guines - border disputes will also work if this is taking too long but may get you excommunicated. Plot to fabricate a claim on the dutchy of Flanders and take it when possible. Once you have a duke level title, plot to fabricate a claim on the kingdom of France and spy on your liege with the intrigue focus. If your liege is under regency or otherwise unavailable, use the downtime to invite some low intrigue characters of a different religion to practice spying on so you can obtain the Master Schemer lifestyle trait. Once you obtain the kingdom of France, you should have enough land to form a custom empire. There isn't really much else to do but sit and wait for the next crusade. If the next crusade targets somewhere other than Jerusalem, check the top right hand corner of the crusade window to see if the target can be switched.

Note that your beneficiary must both completely control the entire county of Jerusalem and have a king or emperor title at the moment you click the option to switch characters - check the county of Jerusalem to make absolutely sure all of its barons belong to your beneficiary before switching. If even a single one doesn't, don't switch characters. Just let your beneficiary's kingdom fall to the next jihad and try again in the next crusade.
Success simultaneously awards "Crusader King" (hold the kingdom of Jerusalem). Afterwards, conquer the middle eastern region to get "Deus Vult" (hold the Empire of the Outremer).

Strategy: Play a powerful tribal pagan such as Sviþjod in 867. Your warrior lodge society will offer you non-lethal duels and the ability to choose the Duelist trait at rank 4, you can easily create rivals by raiding neighbors and taking their wife as a concubine, and if you choose to go the "Ruthless Duelist" route the "Merciless" modifier will negate itself for tribal vassals (note that you will still receive a -10 opinion modifier for all non-vassals in your court). Because duel experience is earned whether you win or lose, it's not necessary to win even a single duel. You may therefore find it more helpful to focus on intrigue so that you can force duels even when your opponent refuses them.

To reduce inbreeding, start with a historic bloodline. Marry a first set of two different bloodlines matrilineally then do it with another set of two bloodlines. Then, marry the two sets together matrilineally. Then, marry a female dynasty member to the resulting son matrilineally. Then marry their daughter to your heir. In the 769 start date, there are three bloodlines very close to each other in Great Britain and Ireland: the Blood of Niall 'of the Nine Hostages', Vortigern and Caradog. The Carolingian Blood is closeby in mainland Europe. The Merovingian blood may become extinct early. For Game Rules , set Matrilineal Marriages to On (necessary to integrate Bloodlines), set Gender Equality to All (easier to get matrilineal marriage and no penalty to female heirs) and Diplomatic Range to On (maximum range allowed for Ironman mode). The Árpáds of Hungary in 1066 starts with already 2 historical Bloodlines. The duke of Nyitra starts with excellent Diplomacy to recruit courtiers, an unmarried sister and a daughter in his court. Adopt Elective succession to easily choose heir. By adding 1 Bloodline per succession, achievement should be obtained at the fourth succession.

Start as Hæsteinn of Retz in 867. Divorce your wife. Form the duchy of Upper Brittany. Pick a lifestyle that adds health so you don't die prematurely. Set your event troops to raid and only use them to raid. Hire the Irish Band and use them to take either Salerno, Capua, or Neapolis, whichever is weakest - you're only using them to expand diplomatic range. Take one of the counties from the Hafsid (Crete) Emirate. Next, take Trinkitat and then Dhofar. Dismiss your mercenaries. Move your capital to Dhofar. Prepare Invasion on the Rashtrakuta kingdom. You should have more than enough troops to win easily - just watch out for the massive defensive power of mountains. Once you win, form the required two duchies and then the kingdom before you die. Your levies + Chinese regiment + event troops + tributary allies should allow you to win without too much problem. Don't underestimate the amount of troops the crusaders can send though.

items.text: Disabling Horse Lords is highly recommended. Otherwise you are likely to face powerful nomadic tribes, and any territories you conquer from them will receive the "nomad agitation" negative modifier which will cause the territory to revert back to the nomad ruler's control upon your ruler's succession unless a certain condition is met. For tribal rulers, the condition is having one holding in the territory with at least two upgraded buildings (which can be purchased with prestige if the holding is a tribe). For feudal rulers, the condition is having at least two holdings in the territory, which can become extremely expensive very quickly as nomads can destroy holdings in the process of construction during their frequent raids.
Start in the "Viking Age" bookmark as Rurik of Holmgarðr, expand and subjugate naturally and then when ready to form the Kingdom use the RoI 'convert to local culture' decision to become Russian.

Alternatively, start as a tribal Slavic pagan (Ilmenian, Volhynian, or Severian) in the "Charlemagne" or "Viking Age" bookmarks and choose the 'embrace Russian culture' personal decision (available by right-clicking your character's portrait). Rodislav Slovensky, High Chief of Ilmenia in 769, is ideally positioned for this.

Consider playing as a tribal Romuva pagan. Eldership is an extremely powerful form of succession (especially for tribals) that allows you to keep your demesne intact upon succession and prevents game over from occurring as long as a single member of your dynasty is alive. Futhermore, Romuva is one of the easiest pagan religions to reform as the holy sites are relatively close to Romuva starting positions and the Romuva tribes begin surrounded by religious enemies which allows for easy expansion and religious MA bonuses through the pagan county conquest CB. Also, the third rank of the Romuva warrior society allows you to instantly upgrade the hillfort and watchtowers of a demesne territory at the cost of 150 renown for each level of upgrade. Finally, as a Baltic culture ruler, any East Slavic territories that you (or another ruler eligible for Russian culture flipping: see Culture#Melting_pots for a full list of requirements) personally control will flip to Russian culture on their own automatically.

content.text: Completing this achievement also sets you up for the "Lech, Czech, and Rus" achievement. The Empire of Rus consists of 5/7 of the required kingdoms to form the Slavic Union. Easiest start is probably Björn Ironside, in Sweden (Sviþjod), in the 867 start because he already has a large fleet.
As soon as you start, pick "Become King" as ambition.
Start subjugating as many provinces as possible. You can easily go to war first with 2-3 of the chiefs that only have 1 county.
Then, you should have enough troops to try and quickly grab Vestergautland and/or Smaland, before Denmark/Sjaelland steal them from you.
Then, turn your attention North and continue subjugating.

At some point, you should be able to "Offer Vassalisation" to the 1-county Norwegian chiefs (typically Herjadal, Jamtaland, Nidaros). Most importantly, try to offer vassalisation to Nidaros. If you are victorious enough, you can snowball "Offer Vassalisation" to all Norwegian chiefs on the coast, provided you share a border with them.
Quickly enough, you should have a large realm. Make sure to have only one son, and/or form Sweden, in order not to have the Gavelkind succession break up the realm.

Build shipbuilders with prestige, assemble an army and/or retinues, and as soon as you have 100 ships + ~6k troops, go raiding. Pick Constantinople, Krete, Malta, Venice, as they typically have a high wealth to fort level ratio.

Important note: The Aztecs will use the tribal invasion CB and randomly land in one of the following counties: Vestisland, Connacht, Innse Gall, Cornwall, Cornouaille, Bordeaux, Coruna, Silves, Tangier, or Anti-Atlus. If the player holds almost all western lands (e.g. as the Roman Empire or any other big empire) and follows any pagan religion (reformed or unreformed), the Aztecs will not attack due to the tribal invasion CB. The Aztecs will still arrive with their units and the player will still get the events such as the disease event, but they will not declare war. Make sure to follow (openly) any non-pagan religion and they will (hopefully) declare war upon landing.

If the Aztecs still land without attacking, convert to any pagan religion (as Aztecs will refuse any diplomatic requests from non-pagans), invite the heir to the Aztec Empire to your court, and land him. When the current Aztec emperor dies, the Empire will become landed. You may convert back to your original religion once the heir is in your court, but you will need to convert back to paganism if the heir dies before the emperor does. Note that this will only work if the heir is a son of the current ruler.

Must become immortal first. See the "There Can Only Be One" achievement.

Then there are five different ways. You can imprison vassals until they revolt, and surrender, thus abdicating to your heir. Plot to kill your immortal predecessor. The second way is to kill the mystic by whom you achieved immortality (the mystic will also gain the immortal trait if you are successful in the immortality event chain). Thirdly, one can develop the lunatic trait (easy through scholarship focus and following the Necronomicon event chain when building an observatory). When a lunatic you have the chance of obtaining Glitterhoof, and then an event appear where you have the option of sharing your blood with your horse. This makes Glitterhoof immortal, whom you can then imprison and execute without lessening public opinion. The fourth, most unlikely option is to wait for the immortal rival event chain to randomly occur, then kill your rival. The fifth option is to turn supernatural events to unrestricted in the game rules (allowing AI's to receive the immortality event chain), this will be highly unlikely to result in a successful immortality, but is worth turning on just on the off chance.

items.text: Your ultimate goal is to become the Emperor of the Arabian (Abbasid) Empire by obtaining a king level title, fabricating a claim on your liege's title, imprisoning your liege, pressing your claim, and instantly winning the 'war'. Begin by picking theology focus for more piety. Expand to the south, capturing enough territory to form the Kingdom of Jerusalem. Be sure to capture Jerusalem itself so you can easily switch between Islam and Christianity: you will need to do so in order to form the Kingdom of Jerusalem, and you will want to immediately switch back to Sunni after forming the kingdom since there's no reason to remain Christian. If capturing Jerusalem is not an option, your inital capital of Sur and the neighboring county of Acre begin as Monothelite and Orthodox, respectively. Furthermore, if Conclave is enabled the "Acquire Title" ambition will likely see the Caliph grant you one of his demense counties, all of which besides Baghdad are Nestorian. With a king-level title, you can now fabricate a plot on your liege's emperor-level title. If the plot fails, simply re-invite the plotters and try again. Once the plot succeeds and you're given a strong claim on the empire, you can now start a faction to install yourself as Emperor. During this time, you should be spying on the Caliph. Attempt to have him abducted whenever possible. Once the Caliph is imprisoned, demand to be installed as Emperor. The Caliph will likely refuse, but you will win the 'war' instantly due to having them imprisoned. Finally, you're a servant no more. If you wish to continue the game, repeated use of the Satanist "Dark Healing" power can remove the eunuch trait.

With a minimum intrigue of 16 (base + education + Intrigue focus ), Mu'nis has a decent chance at successfully completing the immortality quest through the intrigue option. Be warned: failure at the third stage leads to instant death!

Alternatively, attempt to form the Empire of Abyssinia. A quick strategy is to expand into East Africa since it is fragmented. Try to first fabricate a claim on Trinkitat (in Blemmyia). Pick Theology focus for more Piety. Seek opportunity to invade Egypt when you have enough gold (preferably more than 2500) for hiring mercenaries. Finally, become independent and create the title.

Before starting the game, disable Horse Lords. The steppe is going to be one of your primary targets. Disable major Chinese invasions as well - there is no possible way you can beat them.

Start as the duke of Jiuquan in 867. Break free of being a Chinese tributary. Switch to Primogeniture. Invite an unmarried female Hindu to your court and take her as a concubine. Stockpile piety until you have 250 and can convert religions. Secretly and publicly convert. Begin raiding China if you wish, but be forewarned that eventually China will force you to become a tributary and drop an attrition-free stack the size of your total army (as shown on your character screen) directly on Jiuquan if you refuse. Eat up the Nestorian duchy of Qocho to your west and the Taoist duchy of Minyak to your south with holy wars - no one will help them. Take over the relatively weak steppe while you build up strength to fight the much stronger Muslims to your west and the Bon pagans to your south. Build up a light skirmish retinue and holy war your way to victory.

Alternatively, start as Lu Yang of Yopurga in 769, vassal of Kashgar. Immediately antagonize and set war focus to rush a duel, becoming Kashgar's rival is priority. Note if Ferghana's emir has martial education, he will holy war and subjugate you, complicating this strategy and may require a restart. Since your character is set to level 2 martial education with 10 base martial, being put on war focus should put you way above Kashgar's duel ability. Once you've killed Kashgar, either through dueling or assassination, declare war on Uchturpan for the county of Uchturpan, providing you with a castle town and stables. You can also invite Chinese warlords to your realm, since other characters also spawn with martial education and 10 base martial, almost always joining due to their county claims. After this war, prepare to invade neighbouring Ferghana in order to border Transoxania by converting to Buddhism and using a holy war. Note that Ferghana is a tributary of Transoxania, and that Karluks will raid, so wait for a perfect opportunity to invade. This should set you up closer to the Abbasid caliphate with the end goal of invading through Transoxania. Swearing fealty and converting will be best to prepare a takover of the Abbasids. Prepare to place your princess claimant by using favours to force powerful vassals to support your faction, and expanding inside the Abbasids themselves. You can kill your wife if you want your family to be secured on the Abbasid throne once she has a son.

The first challenge is finding the county of Mohadavasaka - it's in western India on the border of Pratihara and Chawda.

Restart until you get a character with high martial. Before unpausing, resign if you're a commander or part of your liege's council so you don't get killed in battle. Immediately divorce your wife and use the character finder to marry someone with high stewardship. Join the Hindu society. Unpause. Next, take the title of your vassal with a castle.

First, try plotting to kill him. The plot doesn't actually need to succeed - as long as you have at least one other plotter the plot will eventually be revealed to the target, who will then become a foe that you can duel and kill. If this is taking too long, you can always simply imprison and execute the vassal, but if imprisonment fails and the vassal chooses rebellion, the vassal can easily defeat you by not raising his levy and just waiting out the warscore timer - it is extremely unlikely that your levy will outnumber both your vassal's levy and garrison in the event of a siege.

You will want to switch cultures ASAP. Indian rulers can subjugate other rulers within the same group for 500 karma every 100 years per character (unlimited for de jure counties of [X kingdom] if 'Become King of [X]' ambition is set) and if a country flips to your Iranian culture, you will be unable to use the War Elephant Pens cultural building of the Indo-Aryan/Dravidian groups that all of India uses (the Iranian cultural building is the Riding Grounds). Besides Nepali, which can always raid, the differences between Indo-Aryan/Dravidian, and your Iranian culture are based on Culture group which Iranian cultured provinces will be limited in the initial conquests. This also helps in providing you with better relations with other Indo-Aryan/Dravidian characters and keeping cultural buildings rather than Iranian cultural buildings.

Raid the Chawda to finance constructing your demesne. Eat up the Pratihara (and the Chawda, if the Pratihara don't force them to become a tributary) with border dispute wars. In the meantime, watch for crown authority to be raised and switch to ultimogeniture succession if it does. Regencies can be dull but it beats having your hard-won realm split apart.
From here, you have two options:

1) Usurp or form a duchy, plot to fabricate a claim on the Pratihara kingdom, form a faction to install yourself, and, if possible - spy on your liege, have them kidnapped, then issue your demand and instantly win the war (otherwise issue your demand and fight your liege as usual). Get your state diplomacy as high as possible to attract more plotters. Note that to plot a claim on your liege's title, your primary title must be a duchy that is de jure within your lieges kingdom, which is initally the very small de jure kingdom of Malwa. Your liege controls enough territory at the start to form Rajputana, but you may need to send him gold (375 + 200 piety) until he has enough to do so.
or 2) Declare independence - not ideal but may be your only choice if option 1 is unfeasible.

After gaining independence, your next goal is to convert to Islam. You will lose your caste once you do so, giving you a large opinion malus with all Hindus, so be sure you can handle the very real possibility of all your vassals revolting simultaneously. Once you're strong enough to resist your neighbors (don't forget to look at their wealth to account for any mercenaries they might hire), raid the Sunnis to your west for a concubine and convert to her religion. You will lose the ability to raid, but the county conquest CB makes this achievement go much faster. The Abbasids and Tagbahlids are close enough that they should assist you in the event of a defensive holy war.

Once you become Muslim, pass the medium crown authority law. Revoke all non-Sunni vassals and replace them with more loyal ones, ideally with high martial to give you more levies. Use 'Promote commander' in the intrigue menu to generate good candidates. If you can't afford that, using the 'raise new vassal' option on a city, temple, or castle that you own will create a new noble of your culture and religion.

3 of the counties you need to complete Khotan are owned by the Western Protectorate. Before fighting them, save and quit. Disable Jade Dragon so you don't have to fight China, then resume your game. Defeat the Western Protectorate (they will still retain any tributaries if they had any), then re-enable Jade Dragon if you wish - you no longer need the border dispute CB which is the main reason to leave it enabled in the first place. If Jade Dragon is re-enabled after being disabled, you will lose all grace with China, all Chinese interaction timers will be reset, all trade posts will be destroyed, but any peace deals will remain in effect.
